App details

Lottery Filter

Create and filter lottery combinations using rules you choose, for adults aged 18 and over.

In the worksPlannedAndroid

What it’s for

An offline tool for adults aged 18 and over to organize number combinations and apply mathematical filters. Set required or excluded numbers, use number patterns and compare against past draws you import. It does not predict winning numbers or promise improved odds.

Main features

  • Required or excluded numbers and number patterns.
  • Save game settings and filter profiles.
  • Compare with past draws you import.
  • No winning-number predictions or promised better odds.

This app is being planned and is not yet available to download. The description presents its intended functions.

Features in detail

Profiles, generation and analysis

A mathematical tool for adults

For adults 18+, this offline tool organises and filters number combinations using your rules. It does not predict winning numbers, improve a combination’s winning probability, sell tickets, take stakes or pay prizes. Historical draw comparisons describe the past, not the next draw.

Number structures and your own profiles

Choose a mathematical structure or define one/two separate number groups with range 1–99, how many you choose (at most 10 per group), and how many the actual draw contains. Structure examples are 5/50+2/12, 5/90, 6/45, 7/35, 6/49, 6/90, 5/49+1/10 and 6/40+1/5. Save, rename, edit, duplicate or delete your lottery and separate filter profiles; filters start off, with no factory recommended winning profile. For example, 5/90 means choosing five distinct numbers from 1 to 90; +2/12 adds a separate choice of two from 1 to 12.

Required/excluded numbers and generation

Mark required and excluded numbers separately in each group, then request 1–1000 combinations that satisfy all enabled conditions. A number cannot be both required and excluded. No complete combination repeats within a run; impossible or exhausted conditions report the actual result count without loosening your filters. Long runs can be cancelled, with finished valid results kept by your confirmation.

Manual combinations, saved results and sharing

Select your own numbers on separate grids and check every active filter and required/excluded condition. See all failed reasons, not just the first. Save even a filter-failing valid number set, name/note it, edit, duplicate or delete later. Save generated results singly, selected or all, then copy/share as plain text without any winning recommendation.

CSV draw history and match thresholds

Import your own draw CSV, map date and number-group columns, preview valid/invalid/duplicate rows and confirm. Good rows can be imported beside errors; adding is default, replacement asks again. Set a minimum previous-match count per group; when two groups are active, both must match the same draw. Dates are optional and imported history is not automatically certified official. A combination is rejected when a past draw meets the configured match threshold. CSV separators may be comma, semicolon or tab; review detected headings and choose the columns to use.

Results statistics and filter impact

See requested, produced, examined and rejected counts, acceptance ratio and running time. Analyse imported draws against a filter profile, or inspect how much of the mathematical combination space survives. Small spaces use exact analysis; larger ones may use a labelled estimate and can be stopped. Independent per-filter effect differs from the first rule that rejected a candidate; neither is a winning chance.

Full or selected offline restore

Back up lottery/filter profiles, draw history, saved combinations and settings to your chosen file. Restore all or selected categories after checking a preview. Merging is default; replacing current data needs explicit confirmation. Resolve name conflicts by keeping both, the existing or restored version. Data recovery does not grant ad-free purchase access.

The JN86 draw

Tap the About logo seven times for a drawn lottery drum releasing four balls marked J, N, 8 and 6. They spell JN86; this offline scene is not a generated lottery combination and changes no profiles or saved numbers.

All mathematical pattern filters

Set each rule separately for each number group. Off disables it; a zero limit, where offered, actively permits no such pattern. Controls show only meaningful parameters for your chosen structure.

Separate adjacent-number pairs

Set the maximum disjoint adjacent pairs allowed: 4–5 and 17–18 count as two; 4–5–6 is not two separate pairs.

Repeated gaps

Limit how often the same gap occurs between sorted neighbouring numbers. A limit of one allows no repeated gap; two allows each gap twice.

Shared last digits

Set how many chosen numbers may end in the same decimal digit. Each number group is checked separately, so an extra-number group does not affect the main one.

Fibonacci pairs

Limit neighbouring members of the Fibonacci sequence within the selected range. Overlapping links count separately: 5–8–13 contains two pairs.

First-digit sequences

Choose a minimum length of increasing or decreasing consecutive first digits. A pattern reaching that length or longer is rejected; fewer than three selected numbers makes this unavailable.

Last-digit sequences

Choose the minimum consecutive rising/falling last-digit pattern to reject. The sequence does not wrap from 9 to 0 and requires at least three chosen numbers.

Distribution across tens groups

Set the maximum selected from each natural group 1–10, 11–20 and so on, including a shorter final group. If the number range spans only one such group, this filter is unavailable.

Arithmetic sequences

Limit equal-step sequences of at least three numbers anywhere in the group. A maximal connected sequence counts once: 5–10–15–20 is one sequence, not several shorter ones.

Alternating A–B step rhythm

Reject a sufficiently long alternating gap pattern A–B–A–B where A differs from B, even within part of the sorted group. Set its minimum number length from five upward when possible.

Doubling links

Limit every x-to-2x link separately. For example 5–10–20 contains two links, and this check can apply even with only two selected numbers.

Distinct paired endings

Limit distinct last digits that occur exactly twice. A last digit shared by three numbers is not a pair for this rule; another digit shared by two still is.

Mirror-number pairs

Limit reversed two-digit pairs such as 12 and 21. A single-digit number has no such pair, and 11 does not form a pair with itself.

Square-number pairs and sequences

Set separate limits for disjoint pairs of neighbouring squares and a rejected minimum sequence length. 4–9 and 25–36 are two pairs; 4–9–16 is a sequence, while 4–16–36 is not consecutive in the square list.

Cube-number sequences

Choose a rejected pattern length among possible consecutive members of 1, 8, 27, 64. 1–8–27 is a three-member pattern, but 1–27–64 is not consecutive in that list.

Triangular-number pairs and sequences

Triangular numbers start 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21. Limit disjoint neighbouring pairs and rejected minimum sequence length separately; 10–15–21 is consecutive. Only values within your number range participate.

Geometric sequences

Reject a chosen length of at least three numbers multiplied each time by the same integer of two or more: 2–4–8–16 or 3–9–27. Two numbers alone are not a sequence for this check.

Use, settings and availability

Offline use

The main functions are designed to work on your device without a JN86 account. Ads, purchases and external links may need internet.

Language, settings and help

Choose one of eight app languages and adjust the available settings. About provides privacy information and a link to voluntary JN86 support. Support does not unlock paid functions. Availability is shown below.

Ads and optional ad removal

All described functions are planned to be free, with banner ads and optional one-time Google Play ad removal. No subscription is planned. The purchase screen shows the actual local price; purchase restoration uses Google Play.

Availability

This app is being created. The features described here are planned; it is not yet available to download.
